questions.question: Describe how Nelson Mandela became South Africa's first democratically elected president.
questions.expected_answer: In the election of April 1994, the ANC won about sixty-two per cent of the votes. On the ninth of May 1994, the members of the new National Assembly elected Nelson Mandela, the ANC leader, as President, and on the tenth of May 1994 he was sworn in at the Union Buildings in Pretoria, in front of world leaders and huge crowds. He had spent twenty-seven years in prison and was released in 1990, and he called on all South Africans to work together.

questions.question: What was the Government of National Unity and why was it formed?
questions.expected_answer: The interim Constitution said that for the first five years, the main parties would share power. The cabinet included ministers from the ANC, the National Party and the IFP, with Mandela as President, Thabo Mbeki and F. W. de Klerk as Deputy Presidents and Mangosuthu Buthelezi as Minister of Home Affairs. It was formed to help former enemies work together and to give all groups confidence in the new democracy after years of violence. The National Party left in 1996.

questions.question: Describe two ways in which the first democratic government tried to heal and rebuild South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Through the Reconstruction and Development Programme, it built more than a million low-cost houses and brought clean water and electricity to millions of people, and introduced free health care for young children and pregnant women. Through the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, led by Desmond Tutu, victims told their stories and people who committed political crimes could receive amnesty if they told the full truth. Sport, such as the 1995 Rugby World Cup, also helped unite people.
